# Read Me

If you have any questions concerning this manuscript or R script, please contact Tobias Heycke (tobias.heycke@gesis.org).

## Citation

This manuscript /script is part of the following manuscript:

Heycke, T. & Stahl, C. (in press). No evaluative conditioning effects with briefly presented stimuli.
Psychological Research. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00426-018-1109-1


## Settings data analysis

The script manuscript_croco4_5.Rmd includes all text and analyses to reproduce the original manuscript.
Currently the data is loaded from R Data frames, as it takes a few minutes to load the data directly from github.
If you wish to load the original (unedited) data files from github please set:

cacheGitData <- FALSE # row 57 in the Rmd files

Also some analyses will be loaded from cache, as the computation time is substantial. 
If you wish to calculate all analyses, please set:

cacheBF <- FALSE # row 54 in the Rmd file

## Additional material

In order to facilitate replication of this research project, the following files can be found in a public Open Science Framework repository:
- video of an example learning phase [https://osf.io/eyfxs/]
- python script used for the data collection [https://osf.io/3dn7e/]
- images and sounds used for the data collection [https://osf.io/3dn7e/]


### Raw data files

All data files were uploaded after every day of data collection under a born-open data protocol (see Rouder, 2016).
The data files can be found in the following folders:

- https://github.com/methexp/rawdata/tree/master/croco4
- https://github.com/methexp/rawdata/tree/master/croco4b
- https://github.com/methexp/rawdata/tree/master/croco5

[A copy of all data files can also be found in the open science Framework repository mentioned above]


## Sources

Rouder, J. N. (2016). The what, why, and how of born-open data. Behavior Research Methods, 48 (3), 1062–1069. doi:10.3758/s13428-015-0630-z

abstract: >
  Evaluative conditioning (EC) changes the preference towards a formerly neutral stimulus (Conditioned Stimulus; CS), by pairing it with a valent stimulus (Unconditioned Stimulus; US), in the direction of the valence of the US. When the CS is presented suboptimally (i.e., too briefly to be consciously perceived), contingency awareness between CS and US can be ruled out. Hence, EC effects with suboptimally presented CSs would support theories claiming that contingency awareness is not necessary for EC effects to occur. Recent studies reported the absence of EC with briefly presented CSs when both CS and US were presented in the visual modality, even though the CSs were identified at above-chance levels. Challenging this finding, Heycke and colleagues (2017) found some evidence for an EC effect with briefly presented visual stimuli in a cross-modal paradigm with auditory USs, but that study did not assess CS visibility. The present study realized a close replication of this study, while deviated from it by using different stimuli, introducing a brief practice phase for the surveillance task, and adding a CS visibility check. Overall EC for briefly presented stimuli was absent, and results from the visibility check show that an EC effect with briefly presented CSs was only found, when the CSs were identified at above-chance levels.
  
  
keywords          : "evaluative conditioning, implicit learning, subliminal learning, cross-modal conditioning, awareness"

We therefore replicated previous findings, showing that images shown while a positive (consonant) sound was played were evaluated more positively than images that were shown while a negative (dissonant) sound was played.

We tested whether stimuli were identified above chance in the visibility testing procedure which followed the learning and evaluation phase.
A two-tailed t test yielded that stimuli that were presented for 30 ms were indeed identified above chance, `r printBFt(ttestVis, N = TRUE)` (chance level = 0.1, average visibility = `r mean(subset(tmpVis, correspondingTime == 153)$percentCorrect)`, *SD* = `r sd(subset(tmpVis, correspondingTime == 153)$percentCorrect)`).
